name: knex(config)
desc: Creates one query builder with a connection pool. Call it once per process and export the result, because each call opens another pool.
body: Knex wraps the mysql2 driver, so awaiting a query builder works without a callback. Keep the pool small. Ten connections per app instance is enough for an exam and leaves room for other clients.

name: .select()
desc: Lists the columns of a select. An object argument renames each column in the result, which is how a join avoids duplicate names.

name: .where()
desc: Adds an AND condition. Several calls chain, and a callback argument groups OR conditions so a later filter cannot attach to the last OR.

name: .join() and .leftJoin()
desc: Joins a second table on a column pair. leftJoin keeps rows from the first table when no match exists, which matters for counts of zero.

name: .insert()
desc: Inserts one row or an array of rows. Against MySQL it resolves to an array whose first item is the new auto increment id.

name: .update()
desc: Writes only the keys present in the object and resolves to the number of affected rows. A missing where clause updates every row.
body: Never pass `request.body` here. The body can carry `customer_email` or any other column, and the update then moves the row or writes data you did not validate.

name: .first()
desc: Adds LIMIT 1 and resolves to the row object or undefined. It does not throw when nothing matches, so the route checks and returns 404.

name: .count() and .sum()
desc: Adds aggregate columns. SUM and AVG return DECIMAL, which mysql2 gives back as a string, so convert values with Number before sending JSON.

name: db.transaction()
desc: Runs several statements on one connection and commits when the callback resolves. A thrown error rolls everything back.

name: Router()
desc: Groups routes in a file that knows only its own paths. The mount path stays in server.js, so a prefix change touches one line.

name: async handler with next(error)
syntax: async (request, response, next) => { try { ... } catch (error) { next(error); } }
desc: Express 4 does not catch a rejected promise, so every async handler needs its own try/catch. Without it the client waits until timeout.
body: Express 5 forwards rejected promises to the error middleware by itself. Code written with the try/catch works on both versions and shows the reader that the handler can fail.

name: errorHandler(error, request, response, next)
desc: The one place that turns an error into a response. Express finds it by its four parameters and it must be registered after every route.
body: Removing `next` from the signature turns the function into ordinary middleware, which Express calls on normal requests and which never sees an error. Keep all four parameters even when the last one is unused.

name: Whitelist request body fields
syntax: for (const field of FIELDS) if (Object.hasOwn(body, field)) row[field] = body[field]
desc: Copies only known fields out of the body and validates each one. Object.hasOwn tells a missing field apart from a falsy value such as 0.

name: Grouped LIKE search
desc: Searches several text columns with OR while keeping them in one parenthesised group. Escape % and _ so the search word is treated as text.
body: Without the callback the SQL becomes `first_name LIKE ? OR ... OR description LIKE ? AND start_date >= ?`, and the last filter applies only to the final OR. The result includes rows the filter was meant to remove.

name: Date range overlap
desc: Finds bookings that touch a date window, including stays that start before it or end after it. Equality counts, because a guest leaving on the last day is still there that morning.
body: The inverted version, `start_date >= from AND end_date <= to`, keeps only bookings inside the window. A stay from June 28 to July 3 then disappears from a July report even though the guests are in the hotel.

name: limit() and offset()
desc: Slices a long result into pages. Cap the page size, order by a unique column, and read the numbers from query strings before they reach SQL.

name: .toSQL().toNative()
desc: Returns the SQL text and the bound values without running the query. Use it when a builder produces an unexpected where clause.

name: Connection from environment
desc: Reads connection settings from .env with a local default, so the same code runs on a laptop and in a container. The password never sits in the repository.
body: `import 'dotenv/config'` must run before the object is built, so it goes at the top of the file that creates the pool. Adding the import to server.js only works if server.js loads db.js afterwards.
